committee: CC Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee
overview: The CC Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee oversees Medford’s municipal communication strategies, public outreach initiatives, and specific resident-focused legislative reforms. Spanning from early 2024 through late 2026, the committee’s work has centered on creating direct engagement channels, including a recurring municipal newsletter and neighborhood-based public meetings. Major legislative actions include the modernization of the Human Rights Commission ordinance and the referral of the Welcoming City policy. As of late 2026, the committee is currently managing a pilot program of neighborhood ward meetings and drafting a modernized noise ordinance based on resident feedback.

threads.name: City Council Newsletter
threads.summary: Beginning in early 2024, the committee focused on modernizing council communications through the creation of a nonpartisan monthly newsletter. Members established a rotating authorship schedule among councilors and collaborated with the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Director to ensure broad distribution. The newsletter transitioned from a quarterly to a monthly production cycle, summarizing legislative actions and municipal updates. By late 2026, the committee continued to refine the drafting process, incorporating details on infrastructure projects and affordable housing initiatives.

threads.name: Human Rights Commission Modernization
threads.summary: The committee undertook a comprehensive review of the Human Rights Commission's enabling ordinance to address recruitment difficulties and outdated language. Deliberations focused on membership size, officer roles, and the establishment of a $1,250 annual stipend for members to improve retention. After consulting with the administration and reviewing various drafts, the committee approved a new ordinance setting the membership at 11 individuals. This modernized structure was referred favorably to the full City Council in May 2025.

threads.name: Public Listening Sessions and Ward Meetings
threads.summary: Initial outreach efforts began with monthly community listening sessions targeting seniors and students at locations like the Senior Center and Medford Public Library. These sessions allowed residents to voice concerns regarding infrastructure maintenance, parking, and municipal accessibility. In 2026, this strategy evolved into a formal pilot program for neighborhood ward meetings held in local schools across all eight city wards. Recent efforts have focused on coordinating hybrid technology for these meetings and exploring the addition of child care services to improve attendance.

threads.name: Noise Ordinance Update
threads.summary: In late 2026, the committee initiated a review of the city's 1974 noise ordinance to address enforcement challenges and modernize regulatory standards. Councilor Tseng presented a draft ordinance based on peer municipal models that introduces measurable decibel limits and a specific schedule of disturbances. To inform the drafting process, the committee approved a resident survey to identify top noise concerns and requested historical data from the police department. The matter remains in committee as members await results from public and departmental consultations.

threads.name: Municipal Budget Engagement
threads.summary: To improve transparency in the municipal budget process, the committee developed a public engagement plan for the FY 2026 budget cycle. This work involved designing a resident survey and creating visualizations to explain fixed costs and departmental requests. The committee reviewed results from over 100 respondents, which highlighted schools and infrastructure as primary short-term priorities. A formal summary of these findings was distributed to the full City Council in June 2025.

threads.name: Veteran Housing Incentive Program
threads.summary: The committee evaluated a proposal from Director of Veterans' Services Veronica Shaw to offer financial incentives to landlords who house qualified veterans. The pilot program proposed a $750 annual rebate for owner-occupant landlords, administered through a local non-profit using existing departmental funds. After a review by legal counsel regarding the program's structure, the committee referred the initiative to the full City Council for approval in late 2024.

threads.name: Welcoming City Ordinance
threads.summary: The committee deliberated on a resolution to codify Medford as a 'Welcoming City,' formalizing policies of non-cooperation with federal immigration authorities on non-criminal matters. After a period of public testimony from advocacy groups and clergy, the committee made minor technical amendments to the text. The finalized ordinance was referred to the full City Council for adoption in December 2024.

threads.name: City Website and Open Data
threads.summary: Early committee work in 2025 involved assessing the staff capacity and costs associated with establishing a citywide open data policy. By 2026, the focus expanded to a broader audit of the municipal website, identifying issues with outdated content and mobile accessibility. The committee approved a resident survey to evaluate user experience and discussed a tiered improvement plan with the IT and Communications departments. These efforts include exploring potential redesign projects involving local vocational students.
